claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

## Summary

Unfortunately, **you are not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

### Key Finding:

The main issue is that **you do not live in the UK**. According to the official UK government guidance, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 **and you live in the UK**.

### What you got right:
- ✓ Alex is 9 years old (under the 16-year age limit)
- ✓ You contribute £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which exceeds the minimum Child Benefit amount
- ✓ Alex is not in care, hospital, or any other disqualifying situation
- ✓ Alex doesn't work 24+ hours/week or receive benefits in their own right

### The problem:
Living in the UK is a fundamental requirement for Child Benefit. While there are some exceptions (such as being a Crown servant or living in certain specified countries), you would need to fall into one of these specific categories to be eligible while living abroad.

If you believe you might qualify under an exception (for example, if you're a Crown servant or have moved to a country covered by special agreements), you should contact the Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your specific circumstances.

reasonings: Alex is 9 years old (under 16), which meets the age requirement. The claimant contributes £30.00 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which exceeds the minimum Child Benefit threshold of £26.05 per week, and no other claimant has priority. Alex is not in local authority care, hospital, residential accommodation, or fostered. Alex does not work 24+ hours per week, has not started an apprenticeship, and does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right. However, the critical issue is that the claimant does not live in the UK. According to the official guidance at gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility, 'You normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK.' The guidance does mention that 'You may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant' and references special provisions for those with settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme. However, without any indication that the claimant falls into these specific exceptions (Crown servant, living in certain specified countries, or having relevant EU Settlement Scheme status), the fundamental requirement of living in the UK is not met. Therefore, the claimant is INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.
